name: historical_named_parliamentary_prose_v1
rationale: Historical English written questions attributed to named Lords and answers attributed to named ministers; contemporary official guidance describes civil servants drafting answers for ministerial approval. These source and date checks support high human-origin likelihood without certifying each passage.
notes: This is a subset of corpus-words-v2, not additional training text.
Preserve original text, source metadata, candidate labels and v2 partitions.
Check the whole parent for generation/translation mentions; quarantine for review, not confirmed machine labels.
Exclude whole parents containing recognisable parser-style missing-question/truncation annotations.
Numeric/table heuristics select prose, not authorship; a human may have prepared an excluded table.
All news and translation benchmarks excluded from this strict core.
No detector scores, synthetic rewriting or subjective style classification used.
Publication date predates modern LLM use; captured-version dates remain unverified.
This institutional genre is not representative of general English and is not an independent contamination audit.
